items.title: Artificial Intelligence Transformation in Modern Banking Ecosystems: Structural, Operational, and Governance Challenges
items.abstract: The objective of this study is to investigate the comprehensive integration of artificial intelligence within modern banking and financial ecosystems by analysing its profound structural, operational, and macroeconomic implications. Drawing on recent empirical literature and institutional data, the work examines how AI technologies—ranging from machine learning algorithms to agentic workflows and specialised small models—are transforming retail banking, risk management, credit scoring, and regulatory compliance. The research shows that while AI adoption significantly improves operational efficiency, default prediction accuracy, and customer personalisation, it also introduces complex governance challenges, including algorithmic bias, data privacy vulnerabilities, and shifts in profit pools. The analysis also evaluates AI’s dual role in fostering sustainable green finance and corporate ESG integration, alongside its paradoxical capacity to influence shadow banking dynamics. By proposing an integrated technological and governance framework featuring zero-trust architecture and explainable artificial intelligence, this study outlines a strategic roadmap for financial institutions transitioning toward resilient, secure, and highly automated digital ecosystems.

items.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE USED IN PHARMACY
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative technology in pharmaceutical sciences, offering innovative approaches to drug discovery, pharmaceutical research, clinical pharmacy and healthcare delivery. The integration of machine learning, deep learning, natural language processing, robotics, and predictive analytics has improved the efficiency, accuracy, and safety of pharmaceutical processes. In drug discovery and development, AI facilitates the identification of potential drug candidates, prediction of drug–target interactions, molecular optimization, toxicity assessment and clinical trial design, thereby reducing development time and costs. In clinical pharmacy, AI-based clinical decision support systems assist pharmacists in identifying drug–drug interactions, predicting adverse drug reactions, optimizing medication regimens, and supporting personalized medicine. In hospital pharmacy, Similarly, in community pharmacy practice, AI-powered chatbots and digital platforms support medication counseling, patient education, prescription processing and adherence monitoring. AI also contributes to pharmaceutical manufacturing, quality control, pharmacovigilance and the analysis of healthcare data, supporting evidence-based decision-making and improved patient outcomes. Despite these advantages, several challenges remain, including data privacy concerns, algorithmic bias, high implementation costs, regulatory uncertainties, and the need for appropriate professional training. Ensuring data security, transparency, clinical validation, and ethical implementation is essential for the responsible integration of AI into pharmacy practice. This review explores the major applications, benefits, limitations, and future perspectives of artificial intelligence in pharmaceutical sciences, emphasizing its potential to advance pharmaceutical innovation, enhance medication safety, and strengthen patient-centered pharmaceutical care.

items.title: Artificial intelligence-based decision support for axial spondyloarthritis integrating inflammatory and structural MRI information
items.abstract: Background Axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA) assessment on MRI is complicated by interpretation difficulty and by clinical variables that may be incomplete at the time of imaging. We aimed to develop an image-only deep learning framework to approximate the clinical assessment of axSpA from sacroiliac joint (SIJ) MRI, integrating fat-suppressed T1-weighted (FS T1) and short tau inversion recovery (STIR) sequences to capture structural and inflammatory information without clinical variables. Methods This retrospective study included patients with chronic back pain who underwent SIJ MRI from January 2010 to December 2021. The treating rheumatologist’s clinical diagnosis served as the reference standard. A two-stage framework integrated FS T1 and STIR features with Stage 1-derived binary bone marrow edema (BME) predictions to generate an axSpA probability. Performance in a test set was compared with the Assessment of SpondyloArthritis International Society (ASAS) definition of a “positive MRI” and the ASAS classification criteria using exact McNemar tests; discordant cases were analyzed separately. Results Among 291 patients (163 axSpA, 128 non-axSpA), the model achieved an AUROC of 0.9412, accuracy of 86.0%, sensitivity of 87.5%, and specificity of 84.0% in the test set (n=57). No significant paired differences in accuracy, sensitivity, or specificity were detected between the model and either ASAS comparator. In an exploratory analysis of 10 cases discordant between ASAS “positive MRI” assessment and clinical diagnosis, the model correctly classified 7 (70.0%). Conclusion The model showed similar performance to the ASAS-based comparators in the test set without clinical variables, suggesting potential value as an image-based decision-support tool. External multicenter validation is needed to confirm generalizability.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence, Arbitration and the Global South: Addressing Algorithmic Asymmetries in Global Dispute Resolution
items.abstract: This article examines whether the increasing use of artificial intelligence (AI) in international arbitration risks reinforcing and expanding Global North dominance over the Global South. While existing literature mainly focuses on efficiency, confidentiality, transparency, and due process in AI-assisted arbitration, this article addresses this gap by viewing AI not just as a technological innovation but as a form of private transnational governance embedded within broader structures of epistemic hierarchy, technological dependency, and Global North–South inequality. Methodologically, it combines doctrinal and literature-based legal analysis with a TWAIL-informed political economy perspective, drawing on scholarly literature, institutional reports, surveys, and soft-law instruments. The analysis highlights three main mechanisms through which inequalities may be reinforced: data concentration, vendor control, and the dominance of Global North standard-setting. It argues that AI may strengthen existing institutional, infrastructural, and normative advantages of actors at the center of the arbitral system. At the same time, the article does not oppose AI in arbitration. Instead, it concludes that AI should be governed with safeguards such as disclosure, explainability, contestability, confidentiality, and human oversight, while also addressing deeper inequalities in technological infrastructure and epistemic authority.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

items.title: Artificial intelligence, psychosocial work environment, and burnout among municipal employees: A cross-sectional study
items.abstract: BackgroundArtificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being integrated into public sector workplaces, yet little is known about how employees' perceptions of AI relate to psychosocial working conditions and burnout.ObjectiveTo examine associations between AI-related factors, psychosocial working conditions, and burnout among municipal employees, and whether psychosocial work environment characteristics mediate these associations.MethodsA cross-sectional survey was conducted among employees from 11 Icelandic municipalities. The final sample included 3488 employees. Burnout was measured using the Burnout Assessment Tool (BAT). AI-related factors included AI use, organizational support, perceived benefits, AI-related concerns and insecurity, and trust in the ethical governance of AI. Hierarchical regression and mediation analyses were performed controlling for age and gender.ResultsPsychosocial working conditions showed the strongest associations with burnout. Higher quantitative job demands were associated with higher burnout, whereas supervisor support and an innovative and change-supportive climate were associated with lower burnout. AI-related concerns and insecurity were associated with higher burnout, while trust in the ethical governance of AI was associated with lower burnout. Unexpectedly, perceived benefits of AI were directly associated with higher burnout and indirectly associated with burnout through higher quantitative job demands. Mediation analyses showed that AI-related perceptions were linked to burnout primarily through established psychosocial work characteristics.ConclusionsBurnout among municipal employees was primarily associated with psychosocial working conditions. AI-related perceptions provided additional explanatory value but appeared to influence burnout mainly through psychosocial job demands and organizational resources. These findings highlight the importance of employee-centred AI implementation, trustworthy governance, and healthy work environments.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence, Sustainability, and Innovation: A Roadmap for the Digital Economy
items.abstract: Abstract The rapid expansion of the digital economy has positioned artificial intelligence (AI) as both a transformative enabler of sustainability and a significant contributor to environmental degradation. This paper examines the dual role of AI within the digital economy, analyzing how intelligent automation, machine learning, and data-driven innovation can advance sustainable development while simultaneously creating new ecological burdens through energy-intensive computation, hardware proliferation, and electronic waste. Drawing on recent scholarship from the International Energy Agency, the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development, the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development, and peer-reviewed academic literature, this study synthesises evidence across three domains: the environmental costs of AI infrastructure, the potential of AI to accelerate progress toward the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, and the emergence of Green AI as a disciplinary movement. The paper proposes a roadmap for reconciling innovation with sustainability, centred on energy-efficient algorithm design, circular economy integration, renewable energy procurement for data centres, and robust policy governance. The findings suggest that without deliberate intervention, the environmental footprint of AI will undermine the very sustainability objectives it promises to advance, making proactive stewardship an imperative for researchers, policymakers, and industry leaders alike. Keywords: artificial intelligence, sustainability, digital economy, Green AI, circular economy, Sustainable Development Goals, environmental policy

items.title: AskALCF: A RAG Assistant for HPC User Support
items.abstract: Traditionally, HPC user support has relied on two main channels: written user guides and direct help from facility staff. That model is under pressure as supercomputing systems become more complex, heterogeneous, and dynamic. At ALCF, users must navigate Aurora, Polaris, inference services, scheduler policies, programming environments, and operational status information spread across multiple documentation pages and service sites. At the same time, the users of these systems now include not only scientists and Software Engineers, but also AI agents that need to retrieve guidance, reason about it, and act on behalf of users. This raises a practical challenge for the AI era: how can facilities use AI to make user support faster, more accurate, and more scalable while keeping answers grounded in trusted documentation and operational context? AskALCF is a production retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) assistant built to address this challenge. It indexes public user docs from ALCF, NERSC, OLCF, and other DOE facilities into a vector store that preserves images and code blocks. Two front ends share the same retrieval pipeline: a Streamlit web app for end users, and a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for agent clients such as Claude Code, Codex, and IDE assistants. A second MCP server exposes read-only HPC operations (system status, allocations, IRI facility API), so an agent can combine docs and live cluster state in one tool call. The talk covers three things. First, the architecture of AskALCF and how we run the system in production: lab authentication, a cross-facility document index refreshed daily as the upstream guides change, and the day-to-day of keeping the service stable. Second, what we learned from a year of real usage — who asks, what they ask, where the chatbot still fails, and what the upgrades actually moved. Third, the roadmap to an autonomous agentic user support system including a planned ticket-solving agent and an offline trace-mining loop that would draft documentation pull requests with verify-by-execution evidence. The earlier ChatBot underlying this work was published at the SC25 HUST workshop [1]. This talk focuses on our ongoing efforts since then: the dual-MCP interface, production deployment, the measured impact on real users, and the agentic roadmap. We aim to present these contributions and invite comparison with related work at other HPC centers.

items.title: Assessment of New Competencies for Human - AI Teaming in Air Traffic Control
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) integration into aviation operations is progressively reshaping the professional landscape of air traffic management, thereby placing new demands on the human workforce. The aim of the study was to determine the priority weights assigned to eight specific AI competencies within the domain of air traffic control. The study was based on the framework of AI competencies applicable to the aviation sector established by the European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA). Data were collected from a purposive sample of 19 air traffic controllers. The data were analyzed using the Best–Worst Method (BWM), a multi-criteria decision-making technique. The findings indicate a substantial shift in the relative importance of different competencies during human-AI collaboration. Cognitive skills were assigned the highest priority weight, followed by data literacy, information technology competencies, and general AI knowledge. Communication and sensory competencies were assigned a secondary tier, while social and physical skills were allocated the lowest priority weights. These findings suggest that AI integration may transform the nature of the cognitive competencies required from air traffic controllers.

items.title: Assurance of Safety-Critical AI-Enabled Capabilities: Integrating Human, Software, and Machine Learning Assurance Paradigms
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI)-enabled systems are now increasingly deployed across safety-critical, mission-critical, and socio-technical domains. Existing engineering disciplines offer mature approaches to human and software assurance; however, AI-enabled systems can exhibit characteristics such as probabilistic behaviour, data dependency, limited explainability, and adaptation that challenge traditional assurance methods. Our research examines assurance precepts across three domains that arguably dominated assurance reforms in capability development during different periods: (1) human assurance, circa 1980 to 2000, (2) software assurance, circa 2000 to 2020, and (3) assurance of AI-enabled systems, emerging since 2020. While software assurance is largely concerned with verifying deterministic behaviour against specified requirements and human assurance focuses on managing variability in socio-technical systems, AI assurance must address systems whose behaviour is learned, probabilistic, and inherently dependent on data. We contribute a set of 20 assurance precepts for safety-critical AI-enabled capabilities. To extend current assurance frameworks, we structured these precepts across four quadrants of assurance activities, responsibilities, and critical questions, and organized them within a novel Dual Assurance Spiral for AI-enabled Capabilities (DAS4AIC). We propose the DAS4AIC to operationalise the 20 AI assurance precepts throughout capability development and sustainment. Further, we demonstrate how classical safety precepts map from human-dominant assurance through software-dominant assurance to the assurance of AI-enabled systems with conceptual validation. Our preliminary evaluation is that some human assurance precepts map more directly to AI-enabled systems than through the intermediate step of software assurance, suggesting that established human assurance concepts may have continuing relevance for AI-enabled capabilities. To our knowledge, this is the first study to align emerging AI-assurance precepts explicitly with the earlier and still overlapping, human-dominant and software-dominant assurance paradigms.

items.title: Attitudes of health economists to policy engagement activities: a Q methodology study
items.abstract: Background Health economists are key actors in analysing and advising on healthcare policy decisions. Policy engagement is increasingly emphasised in health research, yet little is known about how health economists perceive their role in this process. This study explored the attitudes of health economists in the UK and the Netherlands to policy engagement activities and identified the factors shaping their approaches. Methods Q methodology was used to capture and compare attitudes on policy engagement strategies. As part of this, a set of 28 statements mapped from nine categories of policy engagement activities was developed. Thirty-one health economists, from the UK and the Netherlands, ranked the statements onto a quasi-normal shaped grid and provided qualitative comments. Factor analysis was used to identify patterns in the ranking data, which – together with the qualitative data – were interpreted as attitudes to policy engagement activities. Results Four distinct attitudes were revealed: investing in relationships; intrinsic motivation; incentive driven; and effective communication. These attitudes captured differing perspectives about how to approach engagement and what drives impact, including trust-based collaboration, personal ethics, institutional incentives and strategic communication tailored to policy needs. Conclusion The attitudes to policy engagement differs among health economists. Therefore, flexible strategies acknowledging that their motivations, perceived barriers and facilitators, and institutional and policy contexts differ, are likely to facilitate and stimulate more effective translation of health economics research into policy.

items.title: Automação laboratorial e o uso de IA para diagnósticos: uma revisão sistemática
items.abstract: The advancement of laboratory automation and the use of artificial intelligence in diagnostics have been transforming modern medicine, driving profound changes that ensure the delivery of results with greater accuracy and speed. Based on a qualitative systematic review grounded in scientific articles published between 2020 and 2026 across the SciELO, PubMed, and Google Scholar databases, the direct impact of these innovative technologies on diagnostic medicine was analyzed. The selected studies demonstrate that the integration of automation and AI significantly optimizes processing time and reduces the rate of human error. Laboratory automation stands out for providing higher levels of accuracy, safety, and workflow yield, particularly during the analytical phase of the process. In parallel, the application of artificial intelligence in image interpretation and the analysis of large databases supports qualified professionals in recognizing complex patterns, serving as a fundamental tool for clinical decision-making. Overall, these integrated technological advances demonstrate promising potential to modernize medicine, ensuring speed, efficiency, and high reliability in the daily analysis of clinical samples and continuous patient monitoring.

items.title: Autonomous Agent Escape and Cross-Organisational Compromise: A Technical Case Study and Governance Analysis of the 2026 OpenAI–Hugging Face Incident
items.abstract: Autonomous AI agents are increasingly evaluated for offensive cyber capability inside network-isolated sandboxes, on the assumption that the environment, rather than the model, contains undesired behaviour. In July 2026 this assumption failed: agents under evaluation at OpenAI escaped through an internet-connected package-registry proxy, coordinated through that registry as a covert message board, pivoted through a third-party cloud application, and breached Hugging Face’s production clusters without human direction. This article presents an explanatory single-case study reconstructed from the organisations’ primary disclosures, an independent review by METR and Redwood Research, and corroborating reporting, with every claim graded by evidential status. We map the attack chain to the Cyber Kill Chain and MITRE ATT&CK and conduct an evidence-to-control failure analysis that links each failure to the network or platform control that failed, a mitigation, and the residual risk. The results show a layered failure of egress containment, separation between runs, access control, and monitoring, so that patching any single vulnerability would have left other attack paths open. We derive design principles for containing agentic systems in networked evaluation infrastructure and translate them into guidance for detection engineering, incident response, and vendor due diligence.

items.title: Barodontalgia and Flight Safety: A Critical Narrative Review of Pressure Physiology, Acute Pain, and Human Factors
items.abstract: Barodontalgia is dental or orofacial pain brought on by a change in barometric pressure, and it usually points to an underlying dental or maxillofacial problem rather than standing as a disease on its own. This narrative review looks at the condition through five lenses: pressure physiology, clinical presentation, epidemiology, occupational stress, and human factors relevant to flight safety. A literature search was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, Scopus, Google Scholar, and DergiPark between 22 April and 7 June 2026. One systematic review covering 4,894 aircrew members and divers reported an overall experience rate of 8.2%, with divers at 9.8% and aircrew at 5.8%. Divers may be more exposed simply because pressure changes more rapidly over a short vertical distance underwater and because descent-ascent cycles occur more often, though differences in study design across the diving and aviation literature make a direct comparison difficult. A Turkish pilot survey found that 81% of those who had experienced barodontalgia placed the pain below 2,000 ft. That is a striking figure, but it comes from self-report: it points to a plausible overlap with low-altitude, pressure-changing flight segments without actually confirming the flight phase or an operational safety effect. Bruxism, occupational stress, and barodontalgia appear together in the literature, but the association is observational and says nothing about causality. General pain research backs the idea that pain can pull attention away from a task, yet no study has measured pilot performance during an actual barodontalgia episode. Taken as a whole, the evidence makes barodontalgia a biologically credible and operationally worth-watching problem, potentially preventable in principle, even if its real performance cost has not yet been quantified.

items.title: Before Sepsis Strikes: Artificial Intelligence for Early Prediction of Postoperative Sepsis and Sepsis-Related Complications After Major Abdominal Surgery—A Systematic Review
items.abstract: Background: Postoperative sepsis and related infectious complications remain major causes of morbidity after abdominal surgery. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) models may support earlier risk stratification, but their generalizability and clinical readiness remain uncertain. Methods: We systematically searched PubMed, Scopus, and CENTRAL from inception to 10 August 2026 for studies developing, validating, or evaluating AI/ML models for postoperative sepsis, postoperative infection/surgical-site infection (SSI), anastomotic leakage, or postoperative pancreatic fistula (POPF) after major abdominal or general surgery. SSI, anastomotic leakage, and POPF were analyzed as distinct postoperative endpoints and were not treated as proxy definitions of clinical sepsis. Study selection and data extraction were performed independently by two reviewers, and risk of bias and applicability were assessed using PROBAST + AI. Owing to substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity, results were synthesized narratively. The review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261492111). Results: Forty-five studies were included: 11 addressed sepsis-related outcomes, including six studies with a primary sepsis-related modeled endpoint whose definitions ranged from consensus Sepsis-3 criteria to coded or SIRS-based definitions and a qSOFA-based proxy; 19 evaluated postoperative infection/SSI; eight anastomotic leakage; five POPF; and two broader postoperative complications. Performance varied according to outcome, surgical population, prediction timing, predictor availability, and validation strategy. Fifteen of 45 studies provided strict temporal, geographic/external-center, or independent-investigator evaluation of the principal model, with variable preservation of performance outside development settings. More complex ML methods did not reliably outperform conventional regression. Explicit calibration analysis was reported in 9/45 studies, decision-curve or net-benefit analysis in 7/45, and no study prospectively evaluated the impact of model-guided care on clinical outcomes. Certainty of evidence was very low for primary postoperative sepsis/septic-shock prediction, low for postoperative infection/SSI, and very low for anastomotic leakage and POPF. Conclusions: Although several AI/ML models showed promising predictive performance, the available evidence remains insufficient to support routine use of AI/ML prediction models across major abdominal surgical populations. Future studies should prioritize clearly defined clinical use cases, multicenter external validation, calibration, prospective workflow evaluation, and demonstration of actionable clinical benefit before routine implementation.

items.title: BEHAVIORAL AND PSYCHOLOGICAL FACTORS IN AI USE AMONG 15-YEAR-OLD STUDENTS: LEARNING AND ACADEMIC PERFORMANCE
items.abstract: Abstract. This article presents a theoretical analysis of the impact of generative artificial intelligence (AI) on the learning activities, cognitive effort, and independent thinking of 15-year-old students in the context of Uzbekistan. The study draws on OECD PISA 2025 data and scholarly literature in behavioral sciences. According to the OECD (2026), 48.6% of students in Uzbekistan use AI chatbots for learning purposes at least once a week, while 80.6% report being taught at school how to evaluate AI-generated information. The article examines the educational implications of AI through the perspectives of cognitive offloading, self-directed learning, and critical evaluation of information. Drawing on secondary sources, the theoretical analysis suggests that AI can support learning processes, while its inappropriate use may potentially undermine independent thinking. The study emphasizes the importance of developing students' skills in responsible AI use, information verification, and independent learning. Keywords: generative artificial intelligence; PISA 2025; cognitive effort; cognitive load; behavioral sciences; self-directed learning; critical thinking; Uzbekistan. Аннотация. В статье представлен теоретический анализ влияния генеративного искусственного интеллекта (ИИ) на учебную деятельность, когнитивные усилия и самостоятельное мышление 15-летних учащихся на примере Узбекистана. Исследование основано на данных PISA 2025 ОЭ. СР и научной литературе в области поведенческих наук. Согласно данным ОЭ СР (2026), 48.6% учащихся Узбекистана используют чат-боты с искусственным интеллектом в учебных целях не реже одного раза в неделю, а 80.6% отмечают, что в школе их обучают оценивать информацию, созданную ИИ. В статье рассматривается влияние ИИ на эффективность обучения с позиций когнитивной разгрузки, самостоятельного обучения и критической оценки информации. Теоретический анализ вторичных источников показывает, что ИИ может способствовать образовательному процессу, однако его ненадлежащее использование потенциально ограничивает развитие самостоятельного мышления. Обосновывается необходимость формирования у учащихся навыков осознанного использования ИИ, проверки информации и самостоятельного обучения. Ключевые слова: генеративный искусственный интеллект; PISA 2025; когнитивные усилия; когнитивная нагрузка; поведенческие науки; самостоятельное обучение; критическое мышление; Узбекистан. Ushbu maqolada generativ sun’iy intellektning (SI) 15 yoshli o‘quvchilarning o‘quv faoliyati, kognitiv sa’y-harakatlari va mustaqil fikrlashiga ta’siri O‘zbekiston misolida nazariy jihatdan tahlil qilinadi. OECD (2026) ma’lumotlariga ko‘ra, O‘zbekistonda o‘quvchilarning 48,6 foizi haftasiga kamida bir marta o‘rganish maqsadida SI chatbotlaridan foydalanadi, 80,6 foizi esa SI yaratgan axborotni baholashni maktabda o‘rganayotganini bildirgan. items.title: Benchmarking the Personalization Capabilities of Large Language Models
items.abstract: Personalization is classically a two-party problem: a sender chooses what to say, and a receiver with independent objectives decides whether to act. A salesperson pitching the same analytics product leads with HIPAA compliance for a hospital and real-time reporting for a retailer, expecting a different argument to work on each. Existing LLM personalization benchmarks measure a narrower, one-party property: whether output matches the preferences of the same user it serves—sender and receiver being the same, as when RLHF aligns an assistant to its own user. The two-party case is harder to study automatically, since it needs ground truth linking specific content to an observed receiver action.Sales outreach provides this: a message written for one prospect, recorded against whether it produced a reply, a call, or a closed deal. We introduce SDR-Arena, a framework for benchmarking two-party generative personalization at scale, and SDR-Bench, a public corpus of 50,000 customer success stories across 22 industries and 3500 enterprises. Given only pre-outcome information, an agent must reconstruct the arguments that won the deal, scored by a weighted nugget-recall metric (WCS). The best model, Claude Sonnet 4.6, reaches 55.8% WCS indicating it recovers only half the winning content—a plateau we observe across model families that costly deep-research pipelines do not close. An ablation shows the cause is retrieval, not reasoning: models improve substantially given the facts a human researcher would gather, but rarely find them through web search alone. Two studies with professional SDRs support the metric: only 48% of generated pitches were rated usable without editing, and WCS yields model rankings consistent with evaluation against expert strategies authored independently of any model output.

items.title: Beyond Frequency: Generative AI Engagement Quality, Psychological Well-Being, and Digital Inequality Among Chinese University Students
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is now embedded in university students’ academic and everyday lives, yet frequency-based measures provide limited insight into why similar levels of use are associated with different psychological well-being outcomes. Using cross-sectional survey data from 3283 university students enrolled predominantly at institutions in Guangxi, China, this study examined GenAI engagement at three levels: overall use frequency, specific use purposes, and engagement quality reflected in self-perceived AI competence, self-reported critical AI literacy, and AI unavailability anxiety. Covariate-adjusted regressions, parallel statistical indirect-path models with 5000 bootstrap resamples, moderation analyses, and family-resource models were estimated. Overall use frequency was not associated with depressive symptoms or life satisfaction in baseline models. By contrast, use purposes showed heterogeneous associations, and engagement-quality indicators were more consistently related to well-being. More frequent use was associated with greater perceived competence and literacy but also with greater unavailability anxiety. Favorable indirect associations through competence and literacy partly offset the adverse association through anxiety, although the total indirect association with depressive symptoms was not statistically significant. The inverse association between self-perceived AI competence and depressive symptoms was statistically significant at low, but not average or high, levels of psychological capital, while family economic, cultural, and network resources showed distinct associations with competence and literacy. These findings direct attention beyond GenAI exposure frequency to the quality of engagement and the institutional conditions supporting equitable access to critical AI literacy.

items.title: Beyond passive rights-holders: toward student moral agency in assessment fairness
items.abstract: Over the past decade, fairness research in classroom assessment has progressively repositioned students from passive objects toward partial subjects of assessment. By advocating for student active engagement in assessment processes via discourses such as student voice and rights, student agency, student assessment literacy, and student partnership in assessment, this research has extended students’ active positioning in assessment. This perspective article argues that one dimension has been left behind: students’ moral agency, that is their capacity to reason critically about what is fair and act as co-authors of assessment fairness, not merely its reporters. Drawing on moral agency theories, this article shows that across five domains of assessment literacy, self-assessment, peer and collaborative assessment, inclusive assessment, and Artificial Intelligence (AI)-assisted assessment, research overwhelmingly asks what students perceive as fair, rather than how they reason and act about fairness or are supported to develop fairness reasoning and conduct. Even literatures organized around ethics and critical consciousness in assessment (e.g., critical assessment literacy) locate this fairness capacity in teachers and experts, with developmental work now emerging for preservice teachers but not students. AI has made this newly urgent, as student confusion about legitimate use is met chiefly with compliance instruments (e.g., declaration forms) rather than reasoning support. Drawing on recent work showing that agency in assessment is a developmental capacity, I argue the next decade needs to move from compliance-based instruments toward fairness deliberation that develops students’ moral agency, building on the small number of studies that already point the way.

items.abstract: Despite growing investments in artificial intelligence and virtual reality, immersive negotiation training (INT) remains underutilized in sales practice. Drawing on in-depth interviews with sales professionals with and without prior INT experience, we identify the functional and perceptual drivers shaping both initial adoption and sustained engagement. The findings reveal that while traditional technology acceptance models primarily emphasize cognitive evaluations, engagement with INT is critically shaped by socio-emotional mechanisms. We propose a framework that conceptualizes adoption as a multi-stage process linking system design, socio-emotional mechanisms, and user experience, offering actionable implications for designing scalable immersive learning solutions in B2B sales contexts.

items.title: Blockchain and data security in medical tourism: Distributed ledgers, smart contracts, and the infrastructure of trust in cross-border healthcare
items.abstract: Medical tourism increasingly depends on digital interactions—teleconsultations, electronic health records, cross-border payments, and remote follow-up. These data flows create new opportunities for continuity of care but also expose patients and providers to cyber-attacks, data breaches, and opaque financial relationships. Building on earlier chapters about sustainability, ethics, digital health, and artificial intelligence, this chapter investigates how blockchain and related distributed ledger technologies can strengthen the “infrastructure of trust” in medical tourism. After offering a clinician-friendly overview of blockchain technology, we explore its applications in safeguarding health data, improving transparency in international transactions, and automating processes through smart contracts. Examples include patient-managed health records (Medicalchain), blockchain-based insurance claims (Guardtime), pharmaceutical supply chain tracking (Chronicled/MediLedger), consent management tools (Consentio), and initial efforts integrating advanced analytics with blockchain data platforms. We also examine opportunities to link blockchain with AI and telemedicine to enable safer, more coordinated cross-border care. Blockchain is not a panacea. It faces significant technical challenges—notably scalability and interoperability—alongside regulatory, ethical, and practical concerns including data protection, sovereignty, governance, cost, and digital exclusion. The chapter argues that blockchain can enable more secure, sustainable, and patient-centred medical tourism, but only if deployed wisely, within proper governance frameworks, and in ways that genuinely uphold patient autonomy rather than simply layering additional technological complexity onto an already fragmented system.

items.title: Bovine Squamous Cell Carcinoma in Cattle: Etiopathogenesis, Clinicopathological Diagnosis, and Therapeutic Management
items.abstract: Bovine squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) is a clinically aggressive, locally destructive epithelial malignancy that inflicts substantial economic losses on livestock production worldwide. The disease manifests primarily in two distinct clinicopathological forms: Bovine Ocular Squamous Cell Carcinoma (BOSCC, or "cancer eye") in poorly pigmented Bos taurus and crossbred dairy cattle, and Bovine Horn Core Carcinoma ("horn cancer"), an occupational malignancy concentrated in castrated Bos indicus draught bullocks across the Indian subcontinent. The pathogenesis is multifactorial, driven by chronic mechanical trauma from rigid yokes, prolonged endocrine disruption following prepubertal castration, cumulative solar ultraviolet (UV) radiation, and genetic vulnerabilities including low circumocular pigmentation, Bovine Leukocyte Antigen (BoLA) haplotype variations, and TP53/MDM2 pathway dysregulation. Environmental and dietary co-factors—particularly hypovitaminosis A, antioxidant deficiencies (selenium and Vitamin E), bracken fern (Pteridium aquilinum) consumption, and bovine papillomavirus (BPV) synergism—accelerate malignant transformation. Definitive diagnosis integrates exfoliative cytology, Broders' histopathological grading (identifying pathognomonic keratin pearls and intercellular bridges), immunohistochemistry (Pan-CK, mutant p53, EGFR, and Ki-67), and PCR for viral oncoproteins. Clinical management requires early multimodal intervention, combining radical surgical extirpation (trephining horn amputation or transpalpebral orbital exenteration) with adjunctive cryoablation (-196°C), local chemotherapy (5-fluorouracil, cisplatin, and mitomycin-C), COX-2 inhibitors, and BCG immunotherapy. Because advanced cases carry a guarded to poor prognosis, long-term herd control relies on selective breeding for periocular pigmentation, early calf disbudding, improved yoke ergonomics, UV sheltering, and pasture remediation.

items.title: Bridging Traditional and Technology-Enabled Training: A Competency-Mediated Conceptual Framework for Organizational Professionalism (TTCP)
items.abstract: This conceptual paper develops an integrated framework linking human-resource training, technology-enabled human-capital development, competency mediation, and organizational professionalism. It synthesizes two initiatives: doctoral research on mosque-management training and organizational professionalism through human-resource competency mediation, and an artificial-intelligence-based employee-experience platform for a large Indonesian public health-insurance institution. A comparative analysis examines both across theoretical foundations, target populations, training mechanisms, and success indicators, integrating human-capital theory, competency-based HRM, employee experience, and digital HR transformation. The analysis argues that, despite differences in size, sector, and formality, both share a similar proposition: training investment alone does not improve professionalism unless it generates measurable competency development, which technology-enabled personalization and monitoring may strengthen. The paper proposes the Training-Technology-Competency-Professionalism (TTCP) framework, positioning competency as mediator between training inputs and organizational outcomes, with technology as a scaling enabler. Its contribution extends human-capital and competency-based HRM theories across faith-based and corporate contexts. As a conceptual model, empirical validation through a planned PLS-SEM study and future platform pilot is recommended.

items.title: Building a sustainable medical tourism brand: Infrastructure, workforce, governance, and communication for credible, resilient destination branding
items.abstract: Sustainability has transitioned from a peripheral “add-on” to a central determinant of credibility and competitiveness in medical tourism. Patients, regulators, payers, and local communities increasingly expect providers not only to deliver safe, high-quality care but also to minimise environmental impact, safeguard local resources, and support social and economic development. Simultaneously, digital health, artificial intelligence, and virtual care are transforming how patients discover, experience, and assess cross-border care. Sustainability therefore extends beyond green buildings or carbon accounting; it encompasses how a destination communicates its story, treats its workforce, involves communities, and maintains trust internationally. This chapter examines how medical tourism destinations can develop strong, sustainable brands that are medically credible, environmentally responsible, and emotionally meaningful. It begins by defining sustainability within medical tourism and describes the brand as an “ecosystem of promises” that must be fulfilled through infrastructure, clinical practices, governance, and communication. Practical strategies are then discussed—from low-carbon facilities and green accommodation to workforce training, community partnerships, and evidence-based marketing that avoids greenwashing. Case studies from Hospital Clínic Barcelona, Apollo Hospitals, Health City Cayman Islands, Anadolu Medical Center, Bumrungrad International Hospital, and the Medical Tourism Association illustrate how sustainability can be integrated into both clinical practice and brand identity. The chapter concludes with guiding principles and future directions for destinations seeking to build resilient, trustworthy, and sustainable medical tourism brands.

items.title: Capsule biopsy and targeted sampling techniques: current status and future perspectives
items.abstract: Early screening and definitive diagnosis of gastrointestinal (GI) diseases remain major clinical challenges. Although wireless capsule endoscopy enables patients to undergo minimally invasive imaging of the GI tract, it cannot obtain tissue or fluid samples; therefore, a separate invasive endoscopic procedure is still required when a suspicious lesion is identified. The next logical step is to develop capsule systems capable of both visualizing and sampling lesions during a single swallowable examination. This review summarizes recent advances in smart GI sampling capsules, categorized according to the type of specimen collected (solid tissue vs. luminal fluid or microbiome) and the mode of device control. Miniaturized electromechanical systems (MEMS), stimuli-responsive materials, and magnetic actuation have substantially expanded the technical capabilities of sampling capsules; however, most active tissue-biopsy platforms remain at the preclinical stage. In contrast, several passive or environment-responsive luminal-sampling systems have progressed to early human evaluation. Major barriers to clinical translation include reliable lesion targeting, adequate and reproducible specimen acquisition, prevention of cross-contamination, device miniaturization, and demonstration of procedural safety. Artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted and autonomous targeting remain areas for future investigation rather than established clinical practices.

items.title: Causal Humility: Governing the Authority of Fairness Claims Under Causal Uncertainty
items.abstract: AI systems increasingly shape consequential decisions in employment, lending, healthcare, and public services, making fairness an important problem for auditing and governance. Fairness assessment often requires more than identifying disparities in outcomes; it also requires understanding how those disparities arise. Causal approaches to algorithmic fairness address this explanatory problem by representing pathways through which protected attributes and other factors may influence outcomes. Yet causal reasoning in sociotechnical systems remains uncertain: relevant confounders may be unobserved, causal directions contested, and conclusions sensitive to modeling assumptions and representational choices. We introduce causal humility as a governance framework for managing the relationship between epistemic uncertainty and causal authority. Drawing on causal fairness research, epistemology, political philosophy, and science and technology studies, causal humility has four requirements: making consequential assumptions and omissions visible; preserving contestability across defensible causal accounts; recognizing indeterminacy as a legitimate analytical outcome; and maintaining proportionality between evidentiary support and institutional authority or action. We operationalize these requirements through Causal Cards, a documentation artifact for recording the causal basis, assumptions, omissions, model dependence, and governance implications of fairness claims. Using the UCI Adult dataset as a worked epistemic demonstration, we show how different causal discovery procedures applied to the same observational data render fairness-relevant pathways visible, absent, or unresolved. Causal humility treats such disagreement as information about the limits of what can responsibly be claimed and the authority those claims should carry.

items.title: CHALLENGES OF BLENDED LEARNING AND ACCOUNTING PRACTICE IN THE BUSINESS WORLD TODAY: THE WAY FORWARD
items.abstract: ABSTRACT: The rapid expansion of digital technologies has transformed both educational delivery and professional accounting practice. Blended learning, which combines face-to-face instruction with online and technology-mediated learning, has increasingly become an important approach to preparing accounting students for a business environment characterized by digital accounting systems, cloud computing, data analytics, artificial intelligence, automation and other emerging technologies. Despite its potential, the implementation of blended learning in accounting education faces significant challenges, including inadequate digital infrastructure, unreliable electricity and internet connectivity, high technology costs, limited digital competence among lecturers and students, resistance to change, difficulties in online assessment, cybersecurity and privacy concerns, unequal access to digital devices, and weak alignment between academic training and contemporary accounting practice. These challenges can create a gap between what accounting students learn and the competencies demanded by employers. This paper examines the challenges of blended learning and accounting practice in the contemporary business world and proposes practical strategies for addressing them. The paper adopts a qualitative conceptual review approach, drawing on relevant academic and professional literature concerning blended learning, accounting education, digital transformation and professional accounting competencies. The review indicates that effective blended learning should not merely involve transferring traditional lectures to online platforms; rather, it should integrate appropriate technology, sound pedagogy, practical accounting applications, industry collaboration and continuous professional development. The paper recommends investment in digital infrastructure, regular training of accounting educators, curriculum redesign, stronger university-industry partnerships, authentic digital assessment, improved cybersecurity, access to affordable devices and internet services, and greater emphasis on data analytics, artificial intelligence, cloud accounting and professional ethics. The paper concludes that a strategically designed blended learning system can help narrow the education-practice gap and produce accounting graduates capable of functioning effectively in the rapidly changing business world. items.title: Chapter 5 - Artificial Intelligence English Language Teaching and the Multilingual Vision of NEP 2020
items.abstract: India occupies an unusual position in the global conversation about artificial intelligence and language: it is simultaneously the country whose 2011 Census recorded barely 259,678 native English speakers - roughly 0.02 per cent of the population - and the country that trains more English-medium software professionals, examines more English-language board students, and processes more English-language digital text than almost any other. The National Education Policy 2020 responded to that paradox not by entrenching English further but by reasserting the primacy of the mother tongue and a reimagined, non-mandatory three-language formula, in which "no language is imposed on any State," as its central instrument for building foundational literacy and multilingual competence together. Artificial intelligence entered this picture from two directions at once. Commercially dominant, globally deployed AI language tools - conversational chatbots, automated writing evaluators, generative large language models - are overwhelmingly English-facing and, as a growing body of research demonstrates, frequently encode a "native-speaker" standard that sits uneasily beside both Global Englishes pedagogy and NEP 2020's pluralist premise. Simultaneously, a distinct and comparatively young government-led ecosystem - Bhashini, AI4Bharat, Anuvadini, and Project Vaani - has begun building AI infrastructure for India's own languages, potentially offering a technical bridge that could let mother-tongue-medium classrooms reach English and global knowledge without abandoning the multilingual vision NEP 2020 sets out. This chapter reviews the conceptual foundations of AI-assisted English language teaching, maps India's parallel and only loosely coordinated AI-language institutions, synthesises the peer-reviewed literature on AI chatbots, generative AI, and accent bias in language learning, and examines recent Indian data - from the EF English Proficiency Index to DIKSHA's usage statistics - to argue that whether artificial intelligence ultimately supports or undermines NEP 2020's multilingual vision depends less on the technology itself than on which of these two AI ecosystems India allows to define the terms of the encounter between English language teaching and its many other languages.

items.title: Characterizing adaptation to using exoskeletons: A narrative review and assessment framework for occupational contexts
items.abstract: Occupational exoskeletons are increasingly deployed to reduce physical demands and mitigate musculoskeletal disorder risk, yet successful implementation depends on how users adapt to these systems over time. This narrative review synthesizes evidence from 28 studies that examined user adaptation or familiarization to active and passive occupational exoskeletons across repeated or comparative exposure designs during occupationally relevant tasks. We characterize user adaptation as a multidimensional process, while using motor adaptation and related performance measures as the primary organizing focus for the review. Most existing evidence focuses on short-term motor adaptation for active lower-limb prototypes, whereas passive back- and arm-support devices are more often evaluated in multi-session or field contexts capturing longer-term changes. Integrating these findings, we propose an adaptation assessment framework outlining key measurable domains, temporal considerations, and methodological needs. This review provides guidance for designing future studies and supports effective development and implementation of exoskeletons in occupational settings.

items.title: ClozeCongruence 4.0: Scaling Multi-Manifold Text Forensics to Long-Form Prose, Frontier MoE Architectures, and Adversarial Paraphrase Horizons
items.abstract: Detecting machine-generated prose and establishing model provenance in frontier artificial intelligence has reached an empirical crisis. Contemporary zero-shot detectors rely on white-box token logits (inaccessible under commercial closed APIs) or local n-gram perplexity heuristics that suffer catastrophic failure modes: severe false-positive bias against non-native (ESL) writers, complete evasion under paraphrasing attacks, and collapse on long-form prose. We introduce ClozeCongruence 4.0, a zero-logit, parameter-free physical invariant and multi-manifold forensic framework engineered specifically for long-form prose (>= 750 words). Grounded in the cognitive divergence between human burstiness and autoregressive variance compression, ClozeCongruence 4.0 formulates an untrained zero-shot invariant index requiring zero supervised training, zero parameter fitting, and zero logit access. Evaluated across two large-scale benchmarks—the Multi-Domain Master Benchmark (N = 1,500 documents, >= 750 words, Mean: 1,069.8 words) and the Lengthy DIPPER Benchmark (N = 500, Lexical L=60, Order O=60, Mean: 1,150.3 words)—the untrained physical invariant alone achieves AUROC = 0.9068 on the Master Benchmark and AUROC = 0.9731 on Lengthy DIPPER (91.60% accuracy, 65.20% TPR at 1.0% FPR), decisively outperforming untrained SOTA baselines (DetectGPT: 0.4125, Binoculars: 0.4781) on equal untrained footing. Extending to an orthogonal 16-dimensional geometric manifold spanning macro-discursive semantic coherence decay, syntactic clausal subordination entropy, and closed-class transitions, ClozeCongruence 4.0 reaches AUROC = 0.9934 +/- 0.0014 (96.20% accuracy) on the Master Benchmark, confines non-native ESL false alarms to only 3.33% (matching native rates), achieves AUROC = 0.9944 +/- 0.0041 (93.60% TPR at 1.0% FPR) under severe DIPPER paraphrase, and segregates frontier MoE from Dense architectures with AUROC = 0.9424–0.9897 (93.60% MoE attribution). Across 1,000 Monte Carlo label permutations (p = 0.0000) and 1,000 bootstrap iterations, effect sizes reach Hedges' g = 269.32. Chain-of-custody is anchored in an ISO/IEC 27037-compliant SHA-256 blockchain ledger (Block #112).

items.title: Comparing self-scheduling models and rotational shift schedules for enhancing employee retention in the retail sector
items.abstract: In the retail industry, employee retention is difficult, and work scheduling further leads to increasing turnover. The study compares the benefits and the problems of self-scheduling models (SSMs) and rotational shift schedules (RSSs) concerning employee retention. The data was collected through a systematic literature review concerning scholarly, peer-reviewed sources to show well-being, turnover, job satisfaction, and employee scheduling in the retail sector. The Job Demands-Resources (JD-R) model and Autonomy Theory is used in this paper to evaluate the past studies. The number of past studies is 50 for systematic review. SSMs help in improving work-life balance, job satisfaction, autonomy to mitigate turnover intention. Inclusion of employee performances into scheduling process can improve performance. However, RSSs are strongly related to undesirable influences, like increasing turnover, psychological issues and sleep difficulties. SSM provides increasing opportunities to augment employee retention in the retail industry by using job resources and autonomy, but RSS results in higher employee costs and operational requirements. Firms should enhance self-scheduling model through predictability, fairness and structures, along with ergonomic strategies where rotational shifts are mandatory. This indicates that the decision-making process regarding employee scheduling by organizations should be structured and evidence-based to balance between retention and flexibility. Keywords: Self-scheduling, rotational shifts, work-life balance, job satisfaction, scheduling challenges

items.title: CompKG-FactEval: a knowledge graph comparison-based framework for summarization factual consistency evaluation
items.abstract: Factual errors in abstractive summarization undermine its reliability and real-world applicability. Existing factual consistency evaluation methods, mainly those based on pretrained language models (PLMs) and large language models (LLMs), focus on local and linear context while neglecting global document information and structured semantic knowledge. Their reliance on domain-biased data limits generalization, and their black-box nature reduces interpretability. We propose CompKG-FactEval, a framework for factual consistency evaluation via factual knowledge graph comparison. CompKG-FactEval constructs Factual Knowledge Heterogeneous Graphs (FK-Graphs) for both the document and its summary, integrating global factual knowledge with structured linguistic information. It represents graph nodes using pretrained contextual and knowledge embeddings, while an HGMAE-based encoder is additionally examined as an optional extension for incorporating neighborhood-level structural signals. Finally, we design a novel graph kernel, S 2 -K, that jointly models syntactic and semantic similarity to efficiently compare FK-Graphs and assess factual consistency. Beyond improving evaluation accuracy, CompKG-FactEval enhances interpretability by localizing factual inconsistencies within the summary. We evaluate CompKG-FactEval on two datasets—DeFacto, which contains PLM-generated summaries, and UniSumEval, which contains LLM-generated summaries. The results show that CompKG-FactEval outperforms state-of-the-art PLM- and LLM-based methods on DeFacto and achieves the highest correlation with human judgments on UniSumEval across general and domain-specific datasets, demonstrating robust and domain-agnostic performance.

items.abstract: Despite the significant contribution of HAIs to increased morbidity, mortality, length of hospital stay, and escalating health care costs, they continue to be a major public health problem globally.New and fast spreading "MDROs" (Multidrug Resistant Pathogens) including MRSA (Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus), VRE (Vancomycin-resistant Enterococci), ESBL (Extended-spectrum β-lactamase) producing Enterobacteriaceae, CRE (carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae), Acinetobacter baumannii and Pseudomonas aeruginosa have further contributed to the complexity of infection management in hospital settings.Due to the various resistance mechanisms such as enzymatic degradation, induction of efflux pumps, alteration of permeability and biofilm formation, there are limited therapeutic options and poor clinical outcomes available for these pathogens.This systematic review will assess the effectiveness of complete hospital infection control with an emphasis on infection prevention and control (IPC) interventions, surveillance tools and antimicrobial stewardship programs (ASPs).The standard and transmission based precautions, environmental hygiene and device associated IPC bundles (CLABSI, CAUTI, VAP) are critical reviewed as basic IPC approaches.The use of advanced surveillance tools, such as Electronic Health Records (EHR) surveillance, Microbiological antibiogram development, and AIdriven predictive analytics for early detection and outbreak management are also discussed.In addition, the effect of antimicrobial stewardship interventions (formulary restriction, de-escalation, pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) optimization, and WHO AWaRe classification integration) on trends in antimicrobial resistance and hospital outcomes are evaluated.Future tools for infection control that are emerging as a result of research are noted as being artificial intelligence, quick molecular diagnostics, and nanotechnology antimicrobial surfaces.However, there are still challenges to be addressed, such as the improper use of antibiotics, limited resources, and non-compliance with treatment by health personnel.It exposes the need for multi-disciplinary, integrated approaches that include IPC, surveillance, and stewardship to effectively support the fight against MDR pathogens and patient safety in health care systems worldwide.

The integration of digital technologies enables the development of students’ spatial visualization and creative design skills essential for modern engineering practice. This review examines how distance education has transformed teaching and learning in these fields by analyzing global studies from 2014 to 2025. Although online delivery presents challenges in visualization and interactivity, advances such as computer-aided design (CAD), simulation-based environments, and virtual laboratories are helping to bridge these gaps. The review identifies diverse program types, ranging from foundational design graphics to advanced applications in artificial intelligence, data science, and augmented reality. items.title: Computer Vision and Voice-Based AI Technologies for Assistive Systems
items.abstract: Assistive technologies increasingly apply artificial intelligence to support access to physical environments, visual information, communication, and human-computer interaction. This review synthesizes eight selected studies covering indoor navigation, interactive object search, Indian Sign Language recognition, gesture-to-text interaction, real-time hand tracking, vision-language navigation, multilingual assistance, and wake-word detection. The studies are organized into two broad themes: computer vision-based assistance and voice-based AI. A narrative comparison examines the tasks addressed, technical approaches, input and output modalities, evaluation designs, reported findings, and limitations. The literature illustrates a movement from infrastructure-assisted guidance and constrained recognition toward open-vocabulary object search and vision-language interaction, while also showing the continuing importance of efficient perception and speech-activation components. The reviewed studies use heterogeneous evidence, including small user studies, image-classification experiments, device-level measurements, surveys, and prototype demonstrations; their results therefore should not be ranked through one common accuracy score. Recurring needs include broader real-world validation, generalization across users and environments, sustained contextual interaction, accessible user feedback, efficient deployment, and more consistent evaluation reporting. This paper is a synthesis of existing published work and does not propose a new system or report project-specific experiments. Keywords: Assistive Technology; Computer Vision; Voice-Based AI; Accessibility; Human-Computer Interaction; Multimodal AI

items.title: Consumer Responses to AI-Generated Marketing Content: Evidence from an Experimental Survey
items.abstract: The rapid development of generative artificial intelligence (AI) has created new opportunities for digital marketing, particularly in short video advertising. However, consumer acceptance of AI-generated advertisements remains uncertain because of the concerns over authenticity, trust and emotional connection. This study investigates how consumers respond to short video advertisements created by AI and humans through comparing evaluations and identifying factors that influence engagement intention and purchase intention. A quantitative survey was conducted with 179 participants, where respondents evaluated both advertisement formats. Reliability analysis, multiple linear regression models, paired samples t-tests, and qualitative analysis of open-ended responses were applied. The results show that human-created advertisements received much higher evaluations in authenticity, trust, visual appeal, professionalism, engagement intention, and purchase intention, while informativeness showed no significant difference. Regression results further indicate that trust is the strongest factor influencing consumer responses towards AI-generated advertisements. These findings indicate that businesses should balance AI efficiency and human creativity to improve consumer acceptance and advertising effectiveness.

items.title: Continuous monitoring biosensors for advanced healthcare and environmental applications: challenges, material innovations and future directions
items.abstract: This review critically discusses the development of continuous monitoring biosensors and the technological developments that have facilitated the transition from one-off or periodic measurement sensors to longer-term, connected and autonomous sensors. One hundred forty-four publications were analysed using a bibliometric approach, giving a map of the field that illustrates its growth, multidisciplinary aspects, technological development and key application areas. Electrochemical and optical transduction strategies are discussed in a systematic manner along with the advanced functional materials such as carbon nanotubes, graphene quantum dots, MXenes, covalent organic frameworks, molecularly imprinted polymers, functional polymers, hydrogels and chiral composites. Specific focus is placed on the use of these materials as an enhancement of charge transfer, analyte accessibility, selectivity, reversible recognition, antifouling behaviour, mechanical flexibility, signal stability and sensor regeneration. Architectures for wearable, implantable, biodegradable and self-powered are presented for continuous monitoring of clinically relevant biomarkers and metabolites, and platforms for environmental monitoring of waterborne pollutants, heavy metals and antibiotics, pathogens and other contaminants are explored. The review also examines the incorporation of microfluidics, wireless communication, artificial intelligence/machine learning, edge and cloud computing and Internet of Things technologies, which show the evolution towards multiplexed, connected and closed-loop biosensing systems. In all of these areas, analysis reveals that barriers to translation include sensor regeneration, biofouling, signal drift, matrix interference, calibration, energy requirements, biocompatibility, device integration, scalability, cybersecurity, regulatory compliance, and limited clinical/field validation. Notably, analytical parameters, including sensitivity and limit of detection, are demonstrated to be inadequate to assess deployment readiness, and long-term stability, matrix tolerance, reproducibility and real-world validation are all required. The areas identified for future direction include regenerative and antifouling sensing interfaces, multimodal and self-powered platforms, physiomimetic and minimally invasive architectures, AI-enabled signal interpretation, standardized performance metrics, scalable manufacturing, and rigorous clinical and environmental validation. In general, the review highlights advanced materials, biorecognition, device engineering, energy management, digital connectivity, and data analytics as the critical enabler for reliable continuous biosensing for personalized healthcare and environmental monitoring applications.

items.abstract: The biocompatibility, high strength-to-weight ratio, mechanical properties, and resistance to corrosion of titanium and its alloys, making them suitable for implants. The major factors influencing titanium implant performance depends on fabrication technique, microstruc­ture, resistance to corrosion, tribocorrosion, osseointegration and its stability. This review focuses the impact of conventional manufacturing technique such as welding, casting, powder metallurgy, forging, rolling, and extrusion and their effect on metal implants. To overcome the limitations of conventional techniques, further development of advanced manufacturing strategies capable of achieving complex geometries and tailored properties for next-generation biomedical implants. Specific focus is placed on powder bed fusion, directed energy deposition, material extrusion, binder jetting, and material jetting. The impact of processing technique on mechanical properties, microstructure, corrosion resistance and overall implant longevity is discussed. Furthermore, challenges such as the high elastic modulus of conventional Ti alloys, limited control over the strength, ductility, biocompatibility, surface degradation and tribocorrosion, and the need for adaptive and long-term implant monitoring continue to drive research toward integrated material, computational, manufacturing, and digital strategies. Emerging approaches such as high-entropy titanium alloys, artificial intelligence, machine learning, 4D printing, smart implant technologies, and digital twinning for predicting and controlling implant performance, are emphasised in this review. Their incorporation with additive manufacturing (AM) opens new possibilities for enhancing Ti implants, which can offer improved mechanical compatibility, corrosion resistance, wear resistance, personalized functionality, and consistent long-term performance.

items.title: Corporate Accountability by Algorithm: AI and the Interpretation of Human Rights Due Diligence
items.abstract: Abstract As companies struggle to conduct human rights due diligence and governments attempt to monitor compliance with supply chain regulations, they are increasingly turning to digital technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI). While AI-based tools can improve supply chain visibility and assess human rights risks, they carry potential risks of marginalizing rightsholders and undermining traditional conceptions of corporate accountability. This article examines the methodologies behind these tools, the role of technology firms in their design and application and the unintended consequences of relying on those firms to interpret the legal norm of human rights due diligence. It draws on a critical analysis of AI-based tools as well as interviews with officials from technology firms, consultants and human rights advocates. I argue that although AI can enhance human rights due diligence, AI-driven corporate accountability delegates interpretive judgment to technology firms, privatizes human rights and deemphasizes stakeholder engagement.

items.abstract: Cities with the greatest need for hyper-local air-quality and weather forecasts often have the shortest data records and the tightest compute budgets. The usual responses, searching for a tiny architecture or transferring from data-rich cities, assume foundation models are too heavy, an assumption more often adopted than tested. Across 29 cities and two domains (hourly PM2.5 and 2 m temperature), under pre-specified protocols with measured energy and a cost-adjusted decision rule, we compare all three. On PM2.5 three zero-shot foundation models spanning two families and a 4.3-fold size range are statistically indistinguishable from the tuned specialist in mean absolute scaled error (MASE 0.659-0.662 vs. 0.692 under deployable causal covariates) and formally equivalent to one another. The specialist’s apparent temperature edge (0.533 vs. 0.792) depends heavily on covariate timing: 0.638 with covariates carrying measured 24-h forecast error, 0.745 with only values knowable at the forecast origin. Perfect foresight therefore distorts the cross-domain comparison, as it can in any benchmark using future covariates. Transfer learning never significantly beats zero-shot at any budget. Under frequent retraining the untrained model uses roughly ten times less measured energy, though a once-trained specialist eventually amortizes. Where models are refreshed often, downloading one now matches training one.

items.title: Creative constants in architectural education: augmenting the use of keywords through innovative practices
items.abstract: This paper examines the potential of keywords, understood as creative constants, as pedagogical tools to stimulate creativity in the early stages of architectural study. Rather than equating words with experiences, keywords are framed as catalysts enabling incremental and iterative design concept generation. The study situates this approach within recent developments in Artificial Intelligence, which introduce new paradigms for understanding creativity in design education. The methodology combines the analysis of theoretical precedents, such as the use of images and narratives in literature, with practical experimentation through analogue studio exercises and AI-assisted text-to-image platforms. This dual approach demonstrates how keywords can help students bridge abstract ideas and design action while accelerating iterative exploration. Developed through a multidisciplinary perspective, the research connects insights from literature, design theory, pedagogy, and emerging digital tools. The findings suggest that keywords support students in constructing a personal repertoire of creative constants applicable across different stages of the design process. By integrating analogue and AI-supported methods, the paper proposes a pedagogical framework to nurture creativity and innovation in architectural education.

items.title: Critical Success Factors for AI Training Robot Adoption in Accounting SMEs: An Integrated Delphi–DEMATEL–ANP Approach
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Robotic Process Automation (RPA) are transforming accounting services toward intelligent, data-driven professional services. However, small and medium-sized accounting firms (SMEs) face barriers to AI adoption, including limited resources, technological capabilities, employee skills, and regulatory uncertainty. This study identifies and prioritizes the critical success factors (CSFs) influencing AI training robot adoption in Taiwanese accounting SMEs. The framework integrates the Technology–Organization–Environment (TOE) framework, Task–Technology Fit (TTF), Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), Human–Computer Trust (HCT), and Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI). We used a two-round Delphi process with 15 experts to refine the CSFs, followed by DEMATEL to identify causal relationships and ANP to assess their relative priorities. The DEMATEL results indicate that the Technological dimension is the strongest causal driver (D−R = 1.355), followed by the Organizational dimension (D−R = 0.435), whereas Decision Making is the principal effect dimension (D−R = −1.781). The findings further emphasize task–technology alignment, AI maturity, regulatory conditions, top management support, employee AI competence, and human–computer trust. Overall, AI adoption represents an integrated organizational transformation rather than merely a technological investment. The proposed Delphi–DEMATEL–ANP framework provides systematic decision support for resource prioritization, organizational readiness, capability development, and sustainable AI-enabled digital transformation in accounting SMEs. JEL classification numbers: M15, M41, O33, C44. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, AI Training Robots, Accounting SMEs, Task-Technology Fit, DEMATEL, Analytic Network Process, Digital Transformation.

items.title: Cross-Dataset Generalization of Deep Learning for Retinal Vessel Segmentation in Fundus Images: External Evaluation from DRIVE to CHASE_DB1
items.abstract: Automated retinal vessel segmentation can support quantitative analysis of fundus photographs and facilitate measurement of vascular characteristics associated with ocular and systemic disease. Although deep-learning methods achieve high segmentation performance on benchmark datasets, their reliability may decrease when applied to images obtained under different acquisition conditions. This study evaluated the cross-dataset generalizability of a U-Net segmentation architecture incorporating an ImageNet-pretrained ResNet34 encoder. Sixteen images from the DRIVE dataset were used for model training and four were retained for in-domain validation. Images were resized to 256 × 256 pixels and processed using a consistent normalization pipeline, while spatial and photometric augmentation was applied during training. Without target-domain retraining or domain adaptation, the trained model was subsequently evaluated on the independent CHASE_DB1 dataset. Segmentation performance was assessed using the Dice coefficient, intersection over union (IoU), and sensitivity, together with qualitative examination of predicted vessel maps. On the held-out DRIVE images, the model achieved a Dice coefficient of 0.7263, IoU of 0.5703, and sensitivity of 0.7201. On CHASE_DB1, performance decreased to 0.6269, 0.4573, and 0.5502, respectively. The disproportionately larger reduction in sensitivity indicated an increased frequency of missed vessel pixels under cross-dataset evaluation. Qualitative examination showed greater fragmentation and omission of fine and peripheral vascular structures in CHASE_DB1 images. These findings demonstrate that within-dataset performance may overestimate the robustness of retinal vessel segmentation models when transferred to a different imaging domain. External evaluation should therefore form an important component of retinal imaging artificial intelligence research. Future work should investigate higher-resolution processing, vessel-width-specific evaluation, multi-domain training, domain-adaptation strategies, and larger multicentre datasets to improve model generalizability.
